speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Night Terrors (Sleep Terrors).

The patient's symptoms—sudden frightened awakenings with screaming and crying in a sleeping child who is not confused the next day and can be consoled—are classic for night terrors. The frequency of 1-2 times per week and the lack of daytime confusion further support this diagnosis over sleepwalking or other parasomnias. No further diagnostic tests are required at this time.
